description: a 30-person B2B SaaS company having a bad support week

business.name: Tessera Analytics
business.description: Tessera Analytics sells clinical operations dashboards to hospital networks — thirty people, about ninety accounts, two of which are more than half the revenue. A schema migration shipped on Monday broke saved reports for roughly a fifth of customers, the queue has not been under fifty tickets since, and the largest account has a renewal review on Friday.

cast.name: Owen Baptiste
cast.voice: Writes short, owns problems out loud, and always gives a next checkpoint time even when he has no answer. Gets terser as the queue grows.

cast.name: Rina Kovac
cast.voice: Blunt, technically exact, defends her team hard and admits fault faster than anyone expects. Refuses to give an ETA she does not believe.

cast.name: Sam Whitlock
cast.voice: Detailed to the point of exhausting, pastes full stack traces into Slack, and is right about the root cause more often than the engineers like.

cast.name: Delia Voss
cast.voice: Warm, fast, over-apologises to customers and then quietly asks for exactly what she needs internally. Uses the customer's own words back at you.

cast.name: Hugo Zhang
cast.voice: One-line emails with no greeting, usually a question with no context, usually the right question. Forwards customer complaints with 'thoughts?'

cast.name: Elena Petrova
cast.role: Director of Clinical Ops, Brightpath Health
cast.voice: Formal, evidence-led, keeps her own log of every incident with dates and quotes it back. Never raises her voice and never forgets.

cast.name: Karl Osei
cast.voice: Writes like a pager: timestamps, facts, no adjectives. Says 'ack' and 'mitigated' and disappears back into the terminal.

threads.subject: Saved reports still failing - fourth day

messages.body:
Owen,

As of this morning eleven of our saved reports return an error. Two of them feed the Monday capacity meeting, which is how our charge nurses plan the week.

I have logged: Monday 09:40 first failure, Monday 14:10 ticket 8841 raised, Tuesday 11:00 told a fix was 'in testing'.

What is the actual status?

Elena Petrova
Director of Clinical Operations, Brightpath Health

Elena — you are right on all three timestamps. The cause is a column rename in Monday's migration that our saved-report layer did not follow. Engineering has the fix; I do not yet have a date I trust, and I would rather say that than give you a Tuesday answer again.

Next update from me by 16:00 today whether or not anything has changed.

Owen

It is Thursday and my log now has two more entries.

We have a renewal review Friday at 11:00. I would like to be able to tell my CFO that this is fixed, or at minimum when it will be. Please do not let me walk in with nothing.

Forwarding below — Brightpath's CFO mentioned this to me directly at the conference.

Are we going to lose them? One line is fine.

Hugo

The failing reports all reference encounter_ts, which Monday's migration renamed to encounter_started_at. The saved-report layer stores raw SQL, so nothing rewrote them.

There are 1,140 saved reports across 19 accounts using the old name. A rewrite script is straightforward but it edits customer-authored SQL, which I do not think we can do without telling them.

Sam

Sam is right about the cause and right about the consent problem. Options:

1. Add a compatibility view for the old column name. Two hours, no customer SQL touched, slightly gross forever.
2. Rewrite the stored SQL. Cleaner, needs customer sign-off, days.
3. Roll back the migration. Breaks the three accounts already on the new scheduling module.

I want option 1 today and option 2 properly next month. I am not giving a date for 2.

Rina
Ack. Compatibility view is safe from my side, no read amplification worth worrying about. Can deploy in the 13:00 window.

Owen — 63 open, 41 of them the same saved-reports error, 9 waiting on us more than 48 hours.

I can send one honest update to all 19 affected accounts this morning if you give me the words. That collapses most of the queue and stops us writing 41 slightly different versions of the truth.

Delia

documents.title: INC-204 — saved reports failing after migration

paragraphs.text: INC-204 — saved reports failing after migration
Status: open, day four. Severity 2. Roughly a fifth of accounts affected.
Monday's schema migration renamed two columns that saved reports referenced by name. Reports created before the migration fail on open; new ones are fine.
1. Compatibility view that maps the old names. Two days, no data loss, deploy window is Thursday.
2. Full rollback. Four hours, takes the new dashboards with it, and Brightpath asked for those.
TBC — Sam is counting affected accounts by revenue rather than by number, which is the number Hugo will ask for.
One message, sent once, to everyone affected. Not a status page nobody reads.

"Some saved reports created before Monday are failing to open. The cause is a change we made and it is ours to fix. A compatibility release is going out on TBC. Reports created since Monday are unaffected."
Rina will not sign off on a date until the deploy window is confirmed. Owen thinks a message without a date is worse than no message.
Attendees: Elena, her head of analytics, Hugo, Delia.
What they will open with: four days of broken reports during their busiest month.
What we have: the incident report, a fix date if Thursday holds, and 94% uptime for the eleven months before this week.

posts.commentary: New in Tessera this month: cohort views on every clinical dashboard, and a rebuilt query layer underneath them. Faster, and finally consistent across sites.

comments.text: Any update on the saved reports that stopped opening on Monday? Four days now. We have a board update on Thursday and I have nothing to tell them.

posts.commentary: Shipping a schema migration to a live analytics product is like changing a wheel at speed. This week we found out what happens when one of the bolts was load bearing.
We are hiring two more support engineers, because the honest answer to "why did that take four days" is usually a staffing answer.
